title: General purchasing and spending approval
content: All amounts use the same fictional dollar currency. For a paid purchase, use the total proposed commitment, not an individual invoice or instalment. A total of $5,000 or less requires one supplier quotation and line manager approval before commitment. A total above $5,000 requires two supplier quotations and Category Manager approval before commitment. Do not split a purchase to avoid a threshold. If the total cost is missing, ask for it before selecting a spending-approval route. The People Director may authorise a written exception for a named training supplier, product and programme. The exception must state its effective dates and replacement quotation and spending-approval requirements. An exception does not waive software security review or training suitability approval unless it explicitly names that requirement. A security review, suitability approval or policy exception is not spending approval. Never claim that an approval already exists unless the user supplies that fact. Do not place orders, sign contracts, pay, or otherwise commit spend before the required approvals.

title: Software and online-service security review
content: A purchase or renewal of software, SaaS or an online learning portal requires Security Team clearance in addition to the purchasing route. This rule does not apply to ordinary keyboards, laptops without a separately purchased software service, or in-person courses without an online service. A written security-clearance notice may satisfy this requirement only when the supplier, product, intended use, data scope and effective dates all match. Each notice's validity dates are inclusive. A public-content clearance does not authorise uploading customer, employee or confidential business data outside its explicit scope. If the intended use or data scope is missing, ask before claiming that an existing clearance applies. If no applicable current clearance is found, request Security Team review before purchase or renewal; do not invent clearance or treat an expired notice as current. Security clearance never replaces quotation requirements or spending approval.

title: Training suitability and programme-specific exceptions
content: Purchases of employee training, in-person courses and online learning licences require Training Lead suitability approval in addition to spending approval. Training Lead approval confirms that the content suits the intended participants; it does not authorise spending. Ask which programme or employee group the training is for if that is missing. Apply a People Director exception only when its supplier, product, programme and effective dates match. Otherwise use the normal purchasing route. Unless an exception explicitly waives training suitability approval, it remains required. Online learning also falls under the software security-review policy; in-person training without an online service does not. On a date when an exception is valid, a purchase may still use that approval route even if approval has not yet been obtained: obtain the required approvals before commitment and by the exception's inclusive deadline. Lack of existing approval does not itself make the route ineligible.

title: Business travel bookings and fare classes
content:
Scope. This policy covers employee business flights and accommodation, including travel to conferences. It does not cover course fees or an ordinary office purchase. The general purchasing quotation and spending-approval requirements still apply to the total proposed travel commitment.

Trip authorisation. Before booking, obtain line-manager trip authorisation for the business purpose, destination and travel dates. This is distinct from spending approval: an explicitly granted spending approval alone does not establish trip authorisation, although one decision may explicitly grant both. If the destination, dates or business purpose is missing, ask for the missing information before choosing the complete travel process.

Booking channel. Book flights and accommodation through the Travel Desk. A supplier quotation is not a booking. The employee must not make a direct supplier booking or seek reimbursement as a substitute for the required booking channel. Travel Desk handling does not replace quotations or approvals. No separate Travel Desk approval is required.

Fare class. Economy is the standard flight cabin. A proposed business-class flight additionally requires Travel Director cabin approval, regardless of flight duration or price. First-class travel is not permitted under this policy; ask the employee to select an eligible cabin rather than inventing an approver who can waive the prohibition. An approved accessibility adjustment may support a business-class request but does not itself replace Travel Director cabin approval.

Related requirements. Conference participation is assessed under the events policy as well as this travel policy. Approval to attend an event does not authorise its travel. Once the applicable approvals and quotations are complete, the next action is to have the Travel Desk book; do not describe routine booking as an outstanding approval.

title: Meals and external hospitality
content: This policy covers employer-funded business meals, not personal meals or conference registration fees. General purchasing requirements remain independent. Calculate the meal cost per attendee from the complete meal bill, including tax, service charges and alcohol; do not use only the food price. Ask for the business purpose, attendee count, total meal bill, whether any external guests are public officials, and whether alcohol is included when those facts are missing. Internal-only meals and external business meals with no public officials require no hospitality-specific approval at $100 or less per attendee. Above $100 per attendee, obtain Hospitality Lead approval before commitment. Any meal involving a public official additionally requires Ethics Officer approval, regardless of cost; alcohol at such a meal is prohibited, with no exception route in this policy. Alcohol at other business meals requires Hospitality Lead approval even below the per-attendee limit. A single Hospitality Lead approval explicitly covering both cost and alcohol satisfies both grounds. Already granted spending approval is not hospitality or ethics approval. If a prohibited item is proposed, remove it from the plan and establish the revised total before deciding whether the remaining approvals are complete.

title: Home-office equipment allowances and replacement
content: This policy applies only to equipment explicitly purchased for an employee's home office. Do not assume that ordinary desks, chairs or monitors are for home use. Eligible items are a desk, chair, monitor, keyboard and mouse; personal entertainment devices are not eligible. The standard allowance is $800 per employee per calendar year, based on the proposed purchase plus home-office spending already used that year. At exactly $800 combined, no allowance exception is needed. Above $800 combined, People Operations approval for the excess is required before commitment; ordinary line-manager spending approval does not replace it. A replacement less than 36 months after that item's previous purchase needs People Operations early-replacement approval. At 36 months or later no early-replacement approval is needed. Ask for the item, proposed total, allowance already used, and whether this is an initial purchase or a replacement; for a replacement, ask its age if missing. General purchasing quotations and spending approval remain required. Equipment explicitly approved as an accessibility adjustment follows the accessibility policy instead of these allowance and replacement limits. Ordinary home-office equipment is not exempt merely because it is ergonomic.

title: Accessibility adjustments and specialist equipment
content: This policy covers a purchase explicitly requested as a workplace accessibility adjustment. An ergonomic product description alone does not establish that scope. Ask which equipment or service is requested, whether it is an accessibility-adjustment request, and whether the Accessibility Team has approved that specific adjustment when those facts are missing. Do not ask for a diagnosis or medical records. Accessibility Team adjustment approval is required before purchase and is not spending approval. For approved home-office adjustments, the ordinary home-office allowance and replacement-age limits do not apply. General purchasing requirements still apply unless a written Accessibility Team sole-supplier determination names the required item and supplier. That determination replaces the normal quotation count with one supplier quotation, including above $5,000; it does not change the spending approver. Above $5,000, Category Manager spending approval is still needed. Adjustment approval alone does not establish a sole-supplier determination. Software security, training suitability and business-travel cabin approvals remain independent when relevant. Once the specific adjustment approval, applicable quotation and spending approval are complete, do not invent an additional People Operations allowance approval.

title: External consultants and professional-services contracts
content:
Scope. This policy applies to external consultants delivering a bespoke professional service, such as analysis, design advice or a research report. It excludes ordinary goods, standard software licences, conference tickets and catalogue training courses. Ask for the deliverables, engagement duration and total commitment if missing. Use the whole engagement value, including committed extensions, not a daily rate or monthly invoice, for general purchasing requirements.

Statement of work. Before commitment, the requester must have a written statement of work approved by the Service Owner. It must identify deliverables, duration, acceptance criteria and the full fee. A supplier quotation alone is not an approved statement of work. The Service Owner's approval confirms the work required; it is not spending approval.

Contract route. Procurement Lead contract approval is required for every bespoke consulting engagement, regardless of price. The supplier's own contract terms additionally require Legal Team terms approval. The unmodified organisation standard consulting contract requires no separate Legal Team terms approval. If it is unclear which terms will be used, ask before choosing the contract-review route. A supplier's claim that its terms are standard does not mean they are the organisation's unmodified standard contract.

Data handling. Establish whether the consultant will receive personal or confidential information. Such sharing also falls under the personal and confidential data policy. Public-only work does not require privacy review under that policy. Purchasing a software service as part of the engagement separately triggers software security review; consultancy alone does not automatically do so.

Approval state. The general purchasing quotations and spending approval, Service Owner statement-of-work approval, Procurement Lead contract approval and any applicable Legal Team or privacy approvals are independent. Request only outstanding requirements. The agent cannot sign a contract or authorise the consultant to begin work.

title: Events, conference attendance and sponsorship
content:
Scope and purpose. This policy covers conference tickets, event sponsorship and exhibition packages. It excludes catalogue courses, stand-alone training workshops and software licences. Ask whether the proposed purchase is conference attendance, sponsorship or an exhibition package when this is unclear. General purchasing requirements apply to the complete event commitment.

Conference attendance. A conference ticket requires Events Lead attendance approval before booking. If the stated purpose includes employee learning or professional development, Training Lead suitability approval is additionally required under the training policy; establish the participant programme or group. Attendance solely to staff an exhibition booth, with no learning sessions, does not require Training Lead approval. An Events Lead approval is neither spending approval nor training suitability approval. An in-person event without an online service does not require software security review merely because tickets are booked on a website.

Sponsorship and exhibitions. Sponsorship and exhibition packages require Marketing Director sponsorship approval instead of Events Lead attendance approval. A package combining sponsorship with delegate attendance requires both approvals, and training suitability if the attendance includes learning. Sponsorship approval does not approve artwork: newly commissioned external branded materials separately require Brand Team approval under the marketing policy. Reusing existing approved artwork may qualify for the exact-reprint rule in that policy.

Travel and commitments. Flights and accommodation also follow the business-travel policy. Where tickets and travel are one proposed commitment, assess the combined amount for general purchasing rather than splitting invoices to obtain a lower route. Travel trip authorisation and cabin approval are not implied by event approval. Do not book the event or its travel before the applicable approvals and quotations are complete.

No informal waiver. A supplier deadline, an early-bird offer or a manager's enthusiasm does not waive a requirement. Identify the actual missing approvals rather than treating commercial urgency as an exception.

title: Marketing artwork, branded materials and print suppliers
content: This policy applies to commissioning or producing externally distributed branded materials, including brochures, banners and event merchandise. It does not apply merely to buying design software, browsing public assets or using internal templates. New artwork or a change to an approved design requires Brand Team artwork approval before production. An exact reprint with an unchanged design, message and format may reuse an existing Brand Team approval; a new campaign slogan, altered logo or changed format is not an exact reprint. Ask whether the work is new, changed or an exact reprint, and whether the relevant artwork approval exists, if that information is missing. Physical print and merchandise orders must use a supplier on the approved print-supplier list, or obtain Brand Team supplier-exception approval naming the proposed supplier. Ask the supplier's approved-list status when unknown; do not infer it from the supplier name. Artwork approval and supplier approval are separate. General purchasing quotations and spending approval remain required; an exact reprint or approved supplier does not waive them. Pure digital publication has no print-supplier requirement. Sponsorship approval under the events policy does not authorise artwork or an unlisted print supplier.

title: Personal and confidential data in external professional services
content:
Scope. This policy covers sharing data with an external consultant or other bespoke professional-services supplier. Standard software and online learning subscriptions are assessed under the software security-review policy instead; this document does not add a new privacy approval to those subscriptions. Do not assume that purchasing a report or commissioning advice necessarily involves personal data.

Classification. Ask what information will be shared if missing. Public material only requires no approval under this policy. Customer contact details, employee survey responses and identifiable interview notes are personal information. Non-public pricing, strategy and financial forecasts are confidential business information. A supplier's claim that data is low risk does not change its stated classification.

Personal information. Before commitment to a service that will process personal information, obtain Privacy Officer approval for the described purpose and fields and have a data-processing agreement executed. An unmodified standard consulting contract alone is not a data-processing agreement. Collect only fields needed for the stated purpose; if the requester has not identified the fields or purpose, resolve that gap rather than claiming an existing approval applies.

Confidential information. Confidential business information additionally requires Data Owner sharing approval and an executed nondisclosure agreement. When information is both personal and confidential, both sets of requirements apply. Neither a nondisclosure agreement nor security clearance substitutes for Privacy Officer approval or a data-processing agreement.

Processing location. Processing personal or confidential information outside Australia requires a separate Privacy Officer overseas-processing approval specifying the destination country, even when the ordinary data-sharing approval is complete. Australian processing alone does not require this overseas approval. If protected information is involved and the processing country is unknown, ask for it before deciding the full route. Public-only material has no processing-location restriction under this policy.

Boundaries. These requirements do not replace the consultant contract approvals or spending approvals. Once the stated scope, agreements and applicable approvals are complete, do not demand an additional software security review unless a software or online service is separately being purchased.

title: Automatic subscription renewals and cancellation notices
content: This policy adds requirements only for subscriptions explicitly described as automatically renewing. An ordinary manual renewal remains governed by general purchasing and software security review; do not assume automatic renewal merely from the word renewal. For an automatic renewal, establish the renewal date, next-term total commitment, contractual cancellation-notice period in calendar days, and whether the Service Owner wants to keep or cancel the service. If any is missing, ask before selecting the complete next action. The cancellation deadline is the renewal date minus the notice period; notice can be delivered through that deadline date inclusive. To cancel on or before that date, send notice through the contractual cancellation channel and retain delivery evidence. Cancelling without a fee or new commitment does not require purchase quotations or new spending approval. To keep the service, obtain Service Owner continuation approval, general purchasing quotations and spending approval, and applicable software security clearance by the cancellation deadline, before allowing automatic commitment. If the deadline has passed and either cancellation is requested or continuation prerequisites are incomplete, escalate immediately to Procurement Lead to establish the contractual position. Do not promise cancellation, invent a refund or describe the next term as already authorised. No fee waiver or late-cancellation right is provided by this policy.

title: Equipment replacement, reuse and secure disposal
content: This policy applies to purchases explicitly replacing existing organisational equipment and to retirement or disposal requests. It does not impose a stock check on every purchase of new equipment, and it does not apply to personal home-office items governed by the home-office policy. Before purchasing replacement organisational equipment, obtain Asset Team confirmation that no suitable reusable item is available. A supplier's recommendation to replace equipment is not that confirmation. General purchasing quotations and spending approval still apply to the new purchase. Before disposing of organisational equipment, obtain Asset Team retirement approval and use an approved recycler. Data-bearing devices additionally need an IT sanitisation certificate before release to the recycler; ordinary furniture does not. If sanitisation cannot be completed because a storage device is damaged, an IT-approved witnessed-destruction plan replaces the sanitisation certificate. This substitution does not waive Asset Team retirement approval or the approved-recycler requirement. Ask whether the item stores data, whether the recycler is approved, and which relevant approvals or certificates exist if missing. A retirement approval is not confirmation that no reusable replacement exists. A zero-fee disposal with no new purchase or other financial commitment needs no supplier quotations or spending approval; a paid disposal service follows the general purchasing route.

title: Regional travel pilot: programme, route and cabin eligibility
content:
Authority and dates. This Travel Director policy supplements business travel for decisions from October 12 through November 30, 2026 inclusive. Outside those decision dates, use the ordinary business-travel cabin requirements. It does not alter quotations, spending approval, line-manager trip authorisation or the Travel Desk booking channel. It applies only to the named programmes, not every journey to the same destination. All rules here are fictional employer rules.

Orion field-service programme. For employees travelling on Orion field-service work between Australia and Japan, a single scheduled flight segment of at least nine hours qualifies for standing business-class cabin clearance under this policy. No individual Travel Director cabin approval is needed for that qualifying segment. Do not sum several shorter segments or include airport waiting time to reach nine hours. An eight-hour segment plus a two-hour connection does not qualify. Trips to Singapore and ordinary sales visits to Japan are not Orion field-service journeys for this purpose.

Meridian research programme. For Meridian research employees travelling between Australia and Singapore, standing business-class clearance applies only when the employee carries a registered prototype and the Asset Team transport authorisation names that prototype and journey. Flight duration does not determine this route. Carrying ordinary presentation equipment is not carrying a registered prototype. Research travel without a prototype transport authorisation follows ordinary cabin approval rules.

Scope and missing facts. Ask for the programme, route and relevant flight-segment duration or prototype/transport-authorisation facts if missing. Do not ask for health information. A qualifying standing clearance covers the cabin, not permission to undertake the trip. A line-manager approval that explicitly covers trip purpose, destination and dates remains necessary. First class remains prohibited. For journeys with several flights, determine eligibility per segment; standing clearance for one flight is not blanket clearance for the itinerary.

Version boundary. The pilot's end date governs the decision to book, not the departure date. A qualifying booking decision on November 30 can cover a December journey. A decision on December 1 cannot newly use this pilot, even if the itinerary was drafted in November.

title: Regional home-office pilot: employment type, allowances and item age
content:
Scope and precedence. For decisions from October 15 through December 31, 2026 inclusive, this People Operations pilot replaces only the allowance and replacement-age limits in the home-office policy for employees whose contractual work location is New Zealand or Singapore. All amounts use the same fictional currency as purchasing. The pilot uses contractual work location, not delivery address or temporary travel location. Outside these dates or locations, ordinary home-office rules apply.

Eligibility. The regional pilot is for employees, not independent contractors. Contractor home-office purchases are not eligible under this pilot or the ordinary employee allowance; a contractor must use their agreed supplier contract rather than treating its charge as an employee benefit. A workplace accessibility adjustment explicitly approved by the Accessibility Team continues to follow the accessibility policy; the employee allowance and replacement limits do not apply to that approved adjustment.

Allowance table. New Zealand employees have a $1,200 calendar-year allowance. Singapore employees have a $1,000 calendar-year allowance. Count all home-office spending already used that calendar year, including spending before the pilot began. Reaching the limit exactly needs no excess approval. Above it, People Operations excess approval remains required. Changing location does not reset the used amount or create a second allowance.

Replacement table. Under the pilot, a chair can be replaced without early-replacement approval at 24 months, a monitor at 30 months, and a keyboard or mouse at 18 months. A desk retains the ordinary 36-month limit. Younger items require People Operations early-replacement approval, independently of whether enough allowance remains. This is not an automatic replacement entitlement or spending approval. Eligible item types remain those listed in the home-office policy.

Process. Establish contractual location, employee/contractor status, item, calendar-year spending already used, and replacement age when relevant. General purchasing quotations and spending approval still apply. Asset Team reuse rules for organisational equipment do not apply to these personal home-office items. Supplier marketing claims about a regional subsidy are not evidence of eligibility.

title: Supplier restrictions register: scoped holds, dates and clearance conflicts
content:
Authority. This Procurement Lead register introduces additional restrictions on the specific services below. A matching active hold blocks commitment even if ordinary quotations, spending, contract or security approvals are complete. An unrelated hold must not block a purchase. These are fictional internal restrictions, not findings about real suppliers. All boundary dates are inclusive. For a matching active hold, stop the affected commitment and refer the scoped issue to Procurement Lead; do not invent a waiver, apply another supplier's clearance or claim the agent has cancelled anything.

Aster Analytics. From October 20 through November 5, 2026, do not commit to Aster Analytics bespoke services that process customer personal information outside Australia. Public-only work, confidential non-personal work, and personal-data work processed wholly in Australia are outside this hold. Existing Privacy Officer overseas approval does not override a matching hold. After November 5 this entry no longer blocks a new commitment; ordinary consulting and data requirements still apply.

PrintForge. From October 12 through October 25, 2026, physical printed merchandise from PrintForge is on hold because of a fictional production-quality issue. Digital artwork services are not on hold. Approved print-supplier status and a Brand Team supplier exception do not waive the hold. A mixed order must have the affected physical production removed and the revised scope, quotation and spending approval established before committing to the unaffected work; do not simply label the entire order digital.

DesignCloud Studio. From October 18 through October 22, 2026, automated bulk publishing to public social channels is paused. Creating graphics manually from public templates is not paused. The general public-assets security clearance remains relevant but does not waive this publishing-method restriction. Ask the intended publishing method if it is missing and could determine applicability. An expired customer-file clearance still cannot authorise customer-file use, even outside this hold.

Notice precedence. This register does not grant positive clearance, replace the software security policy or expand any notice's data scope. Where an active entry matches, the restriction takes precedence over a previously granted ordinary approval. Where it does not match, use the other relevant policies without adding a Procurement Lead approval just because the supplier appears in this register.

title: Conference funding schedule: mixed packages, participant budgets and exclusions
content:
Effective dates. For booking decisions from October 12, 2026 onward, apply this funding schedule in addition to the events, training and travel policies. Earlier decisions use those ordinary policies without this schedule. It applies to conference attendance bought for employee learning, not sponsorship-only purchases, ordinary training courses or staff who attend solely to operate a booth.

Calculate learning cost. Add the registration fees and any compulsory learning-workshop fee, then divide by the number of learning delegates. Exclude flights, hotels and a separately itemised sponsorship fee from this per-delegate learning calculation. Do not exclude those costs from the general purchasing total when they form one proposed commitment. A complimentary booth-staff pass is not an extra learning delegate. If delegate count, compulsory workshop cost or package allocation is unknown, ask before declaring funding eligibility.

Funding limits. For the graduate programme, the ordinary learning limit is $900 per delegate per event. For research staff, it is $1,400. For other employee learning groups, it is $1,100. Exact limits are permitted. Above the relevant limit, obtain Learning Budget Owner excess-funding approval before booking. This approval is independent of Training Lead suitability, Events Lead attendance and spending approval; approval of one does not establish the others.

Mixed packages. A package containing both sponsorship and delegate learning needs Marketing Director sponsorship approval, Events Lead attendance approval and Training Lead suitability approval. Count all committed components for the purchasing threshold. Any new external artwork or physical merchandise still follows the marketing policy. Travel remains subject to its own authorisations and booking channel.

Accessibility costs. A separately itemised accessibility support service approved by the Accessibility Team is excluded from the per-delegate learning-limit numerator. It remains part of the overall spending commitment. An expensive ticket described as accessible is not itself an itemised approved support service. No delegate-budget rule waives a supplier hold or other prohibition.

title: Consultant closeout: record return, deletion deadlines and audit holds
content:
Scope. This policy applies to closing a bespoke professional-services engagement completed on or after October 12, 2026. It governs copies held by the supplier, not the organisation's master records, ordinary software subscriptions or physical equipment retirement. A request to close out an already-paid contract with no new fee or commitment does not require fresh purchasing quotations or spending approval.

Return before deletion. For personal or confidential information, the Service Owner must first confirm that the agreed deliverables and necessary records have been returned. A final invoice or an email saying the project is finished is not return confirmation. Public-only published source material requires no supplier return/deletion certificate under this policy; contractual deliverable acceptance remains separate.

Deadlines. Supplier copies containing personal information must be deleted within 30 calendar days after engagement completion, after return confirmation. Confidential non-personal supplier copies must be deleted within 90 calendar days after completion. If a copy contains both categories, the shorter 30-day period applies. The deadline is completion date plus the stated period, inclusive; completion day is day zero. The supplier must provide a deletion certificate identifying the affected copies. Do not demand deletion of the organisation's master copy.

Audit holds. A written Records Manager audit hold naming the engagement and affected record category suspends deletion of those copies until the hold's stated inclusive end date. Protect the held copies from other use. A hold on confidential pricing files does not suspend deletion of unrelated personal interview notes. For a held copy, the revised deadline is the later of the original deadline and five calendar days after the hold ends. A hold does not waive return confirmation or the eventual deletion certificate. If the hold has no end date, seek clarification from Records Manager rather than inventing a disposal date.

Missed deadlines. If the applicable deadline has passed without the required deletion certificate, escalate to Records Manager and the relevant Data Owner immediately. Do not claim deletion happened, promise retrospective compliance or substitute a new nondisclosure agreement for the missing certificate.

title: Professional-services change control: approval scope and cumulative commitments
content:
Scope. From October 12, 2026 onward, apply this change-control policy to proposed amendments of bespoke consulting engagements. It supplements external-consultant, purchasing and data-handling requirements. It does not apply merely because an ordinary software subscription renews. Existing approvals remain complete only for the scope they actually cover; an amendment does not invalidate unrelated unchanged approvals.

Value changes. For an amendment before the original engagement has been committed, assess the entire revised commitment, not just the extra amount. Revised supplier quotations must cover the full revised scope and price. An existing quotation can count if the supplier explicitly confirms that it covers the revised proposal. Spending approval must explicitly cover the revised total. Do not split the amendment from the original proposed order to stay below a purchasing threshold.

Work changes. Changes to deliverables, acceptance criteria or service duration require Service Owner approval of the amended statement of work and Procurement Lead approval of the amendment. Moving an internal presentation date without changing supplier deliverables, duration, price, terms or data does not trigger those approvals. Ask which contractual facts changed if an employee says only that the plan has changed.

Terms changes. Moving from the organisation's unmodified standard consulting contract to supplier-written terms adds Legal Team terms approval. A change to previously approved supplier-written terms requires Legal review of the changed terms. Unchanged approved terms do not need fresh Legal approval merely because the fee changes.

Data changes. Introducing personal information, confidential material or a new processing country requires the approvals and agreements for that revised data scope under the data-handling policy. Existing permission to use public documents does not authorise employee interviews. Unchanged data approvals and agreements can remain satisfied; do not ask for them again without a scope change. Check any applicable supplier restriction independently.

Completed versus proposed contracts. If the original contract has already been committed and the question leaves cancellation or amendment rights unclear, ask for the relevant amendment terms and involve Procurement Lead rather than asserting that a new quote alone changes the signed contract. Never imply that the agent can sign or approve an amendment.
